label: directional/recipient "to" preposition
explanation: Fires on "to" when it marks a goal, recipient, or relation, especially after transfer/relation words like added, applied, access, back, go, available, dedicated, attributed, compared. It stays silent on most infinitive "to" (after "it", "want", "have") and after punctuation; stronger firing follows clear collocates, weaker firing is spillover onto "into"/"with" or unrelated tokens.
